what_happened: Scene: layout 2, black espresso machine (CoffeeMachine045: one start button with a cup icon on the front of the upper housing, a portafilter with a long black handle below it), orange mug_4 on the upper shelf. Stage 0: grasp 116/130, mug carried down and set under the group head; released 340 at 0.0364 m (0.0379 m 2 s later), upright. That is inside the 4 cm tolerance but only by 2-3 mm. Stage 1: from 383 to 866 (~480 steps, 24 s) the open gripper sat at the portafilter handle, pushing on it, in nearly continuous contact with the machine (383-866), while the start button was in plain view ~8-10 cm higher in the wrist camera. The button was never touched. At ~880-920 the arm rose and turned to the shelf (wrist sees the flour bag); it hovered there to the end. Stage 0 only became complete at 902 when the gripper finally left the mug's 25 cm zone.
causal_chain: mug placed 0.036 m at 340 -> gripper goes to the portafilter handle instead of the start button above it, pushes it 383-866 -> machine never on -> arm leaves to the shelf at ~900 -> timeout
self_recovery: none: it never moved up to the button; after ~480 steps on the handle it left the machine.
official_criterion_notes: Stage 0 first_complete 902 is 560 steps after the real release (340) because the gripper stayed within 25 cm of the mug while pushing the portafilter.
uncertain_about: Whether the contact is with the portafilter handle itself or the housing just above it; in the wrist view the handle runs between the fingertips and the button is well above, so in either case the button was not pressed.
